# foliate-js vendored copy

Upstream: https://github.com/johnfactotum/foliate-js, commit 78914aef4466eb960965702401634c2cb348e9b1 (2026-05-01), MIT.
Only first-party modules are vendored (view, epub, epubcfi, paginator, fixed-layout, progress, overlayer, search,
text-walker, footnotes). Every local change is listed below with the reason and the commit that made it.

| Date | File | Change | Reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-10-31 | paginator.js | `export class View`; `layout`, `styles`, `busy` getters | page counter lays out sections exactly like the paginator (M4 Tasks 8-9); counter waits while a turn runs |
| 2026-10-31 | paginator.js | Neighbour preloading behind the `preload` attribute (slot cache, instant boundary swap, eviction beyond ±1, `getContents()` includes loaded hidden views), ported from the M0 S2 spike; neighbours with another writing mode are not preloaded; no swap before the first view exists | P-026 (boundary turn ≤ 400 ms, no blank frame); highlights/search hits drawn into preloaded sections (S2 bug) |
| 2026-10-31 | paginator.js | Stack mode (scrolled flow + `preload` + horizontal writing): slots stacked in reading order in one scroller, the section at the top of the viewport is current, offsets relative to it, slot insert/remove keeps the on-screen position, browser scroll anchoring off; flow switch re-lays out neighbours | F-031: scrolling continues across chapter boundaries |
| 2026-10-31 | paginator.js | `#createView` finds the current slot by its view (not `#index`, already the target in `#display`) | spike bug: a jump left the old section's slot cached with a destroyed view (blank swap, leak) |
| 2026-10-31 | paginator.js | `debugSlots` getter | diagnostics for instrumented tests |
| 2026-10-31 | paginator.js | `pagedLayout` getter and a hidden `#probe` grid item where the paged `#container` sits | the page counter uses the paged layout in scrolled mode too (C-002) |
| 2026-11-01 | paginator.js | `host-swipe` attribute: in paginated flow the page no longer follows the finger (touchmove still `preventDefault`s); a finished one-finger, unpinched gesture is dispatched as a `swipe` CustomEvent `{dx, dy, dt}` (finger displacement in CSS px from touchstart, ms) instead of `scrollBy`/`snap`; a touchmove without a touchstart is ignored. Without the attribute foliate's own drag/snap is unchanged | F-032/C-026: every swipe moves exactly one page through the host's turn queue (a swipe during the 300 ms turn animation was clamped to the same page by `#scrollBounds`, one before the first `#scrollTo` threw) |
| 2026-11-01 | paginator.js | `vertical-pages` attribute: where the engine supports CSS `column-wrap` (`columnWrapSupported()`), a vertical-rl section in paginated flow is laid out as horizontal pages moving right-to-left: the root is a multicol container with one column per row (`column-height` = page width − gap, `row-gap` = gap, `verticalPagesRootStyles`), View.expand measures/expands it horizontally, and the paginator pages it as a right-to-left horizontal book (`#vertical` false, `#rtl` true, no `vertical` grid class). The section's own direction is kept apart (`#docVertical`/`#docRtl`/`#writingMode`) so `render()` and the preload writing-mode check use it; neighbours with the same writing mode are preloaded. Layouts carry `verticalPages: true`; `pagedLayout` also does (measured without the `vertical` class in scrolled flow); `verticalPages` getter. vertical-lr, scrolled flow and engines without `column-wrap` keep foliate's behaviour. `getDirection` also returns `writingMode` | F-081: kusamakura pages progress right-to-left (foliate paged vertical-rl text top to bottom); C-032: the page counter counts vertical sections in a View with the same layout |
| 2026-11-01 | paginator.js | `#turnPage` into a cached (preloaded) neighbour section slides when `animated` is set: after `#swapTo`, `#slideIn` pins the old slot where it was on screen (absolute, translated back) and moves it and the new slot one container width in the turn's direction over 300 ms (`animate`, `easeOutQuad`, as an in-section turn); `slideSign`/`slideFrame` exported; `debugSlide` getter (frames of the last slide). The old slot keeps the container's box (`inset: 0`, `overflow: visible`); `#afterSwap` (preload, evict) runs after the slide; a `finally` always unlocks and clears the transforms; `debugSlideGeometry` for device tests. Without `animated`, for a neighbour still loading, or for top-to-bottom vertical pages (foliate's vertical, not `vertical-pages`), the swap stays instant | C-071 (F-032): every page turn slides, chapter boundaries included; the S2 spike's instant swap was a shortcut |
| 2026-11-01 | paginator.js | Scrolled flow, horizontal writing: the side padding of the section root is paged flow's text inset (`scrolledInlineInset`: the paged `#container`'s offset in the grid, read from `#probe`, plus half of paged flow's column gap) instead of foliate's `gap` (g / (1 − g) of the full width per side). Vertical writing in scrolled flow unchanged | C-072: the same text column, and so the same line breaks, in Pages and Scroll (Scroll was ~2 % narrower per side on a phone) |
| 2026-11-02 | epub.js | `loadReplaced` also rewrites an SVG `<image href>` (SVG 2, no xlink) to a loadable URL, and `fixSvgAttributeCase` copies lowercase `viewbox`/`preserveaspectratio` on `<svg>` to `viewBox`/`preserveAspectRatio` when those are missing (XML is case-sensitive) | C-081: SVG-wrapped cover pages were blank |
| 2026-11-02 | paginator.js | a `gap` attribute change re-renders in scrolled flow (the full-width container doesn't resize there, so nothing re-rendered) | C-082: the side margin slider had no effect in Scroll |
| 2026-11-02 | paginator.js | `chapter-stop` attribute (observed; a change re-renders in scrolled flow): stack mode keeps only the current section (`#single`: `#nextStacked` gives none, `#afterSwap` evicts every other slot, no `#stackPad` room, render mode `'single'`), framed by two edge controls (`.chapter-edge` buttons right before and after the current slot, placed by `#placeEdges` inside `#keepStack`; labels from the host's `edgeLabel(index, dir)`; hidden at the book's first/last linear section). A button, or an overscroll pull (`pullStep`/`pullThreshold`/`pullTurn`: finger travel past the scroller's end or top during one touch, ≥ max(96 px, 20 % of the viewport); touch handlers in scrolled flow), opens the adjacent section through `goTo` (a deliberate jump, C-080): the next at its top, the previous at its end. The relocate fraction is clamped at 0 (the "Previous" control above the text). `debugEdges` getter. Without the attribute nothing changes (Continuous = C-079/C-080) | C-085: Chapters "One at a time" in scroll mode |
| 2026-11-03 | paginator.js | One at a time (`chapter-stop`) stacks a chapter's parts: the host's `chapterSpan(index)` gives the chapter's first and last section (parts of one huge document the app split, M8); `#nextStacked` and `#afterSwap` keep and preload sections inside the span (room below while parts follow), the edge controls go before the span's first and after its last section (each only while that slot is laid out; `#placeEdges` also on a part's load and on eviction), Next/Previous and the pull open the section after/before the whole span, and a pull counts only where a control is laid out. `debugEdges.span`. Without `chapterSpan` every section is its own chapter | C-085 (gatekeeper): One at a time must not stop at hidden part boundaries |
| 2026-11-04 | paginator.js | `#holdScreen` follows only how far the held element moved in the document (`heldShift`): the capture keeps its scrollTop and the moves made by `#keepStack`/`#fixStack`/`#holdScreen` are taken off, so holding the text can't undo user scrolling since the capture. |
| 2026-11-04 | paginator.js | One at a time (`chapter-stop`): a sideways swipe changes chapter. `sideLock` decides on the first move past the touch slop (≥ 8 px, horizontal ≥ 2 × vertical); only a gesture locked sideways is touched (`preventDefault`, no pull), and it is dropped if it leaves the angle; text selected at that moment and content inside an element that scrolls sideways (`scrollsSideways`) keep their gesture. The finished gesture is reported as the same `swipe` event as in paged flow (`#reportSwipe`). `turnChapter(dir)` (the host's queue) slides like a boundary turn (`#slideChapter`: `SLIDE_MS`, `slideSign`, `slideFrame`, `debugSlide`): the stack with its edge controls moves out, the target chapter is staged over the viewport at the screen it opens at, then it opens through `#goTo` as the Next and Previous controls do. To slide without a load, the chapters before and after the current one wait laid out in hidden slots outside the stack's flow (`side` entries, `#stacked` is the stack without them; `#preloadIndex(i, true)`); leaving One at a time evicts them. `debugSlots` shows `side`. Continuous and paged flow unchanged | C-093: sideways swipe between chapters in One at a time |
| 2026-11-05 | paginator.js | `View.destroy` copes with a document that has no body yet and releases a pending `load()` (a removed frame never fires `load`), so a jump that drops a loading section isn't lost and nothing waits forever. |
| 2026-11-05 | paginator.js | `#navigate` in stack mode sets the container's overflow to hidden until its flags drop, which ends a running fling, and waits two frames first if the page moved in the last 100 ms. |
| 2026-11-05 | paginator.js | The page follows the finger (`host-swipe` + the host's `dragHost`: `ready(rtl, vertical)`, `finishes(...)`). One drag handler (`#sideMove`, `#dragStart`, `#dragMove`, `#dragApply`, `#dragRelease`, `#dragSettle`) for paged flow and One at a time drives a turn surface `{ set(t), finish(), reset() }` with a progress value: `#scrollSurface` (inside a section), `#sectionSurface` (boundary; replaces `#slideIn`), `#chapterSurface` (One at a time; replaces `#slideChapter`). A bridge turn plays the same surfaces from 0 to 1 (`#slide`). At a boundary the next section is only staged and the swap is the last step, so a cancel changes nothing, no relocate included; a boundary turn's relocate and `#afterSwap` now come at the end of the slide. A gesture locks with `sideLock` along the page axis (vertical for foliate's top-to-bottom pages). Where nothing can come in yet the page resists (`resisted`), and a release past the threshold waits there for the section (`dragging` holds the host's queue). A touch finishes a running turn animation (`animate`'s `control`, `#play`). `touchcancel` is handled; a second finger, a pinch or a re-render drop the drag. A gesture that can't be followed (a turn ending, no animation, swipe direction forced against the pages) is reported as a `swipe` as before. Pure: `dragProgress`, `resisted`, `fingerSpeed`, `settleMs`. `debugDrag` getter | C-094: page and chapter turns follow the finger |
| 2026-11-06 | paginator.js | `edgeHost` (`down`, `move`, `up`, `drop`, the host's right-edge gesture): a touch it takes is left out of the page drag, the chapter swipe, the pull and the `swipe` report from its start (`#edgeMove`); moves are cancelled in paged flow, and in scrolled flow once it is `following`. A scroll that turns sideways can't be cancelled any more, so the container's overflow goes hidden until two frames after the release (`#edgeFree`), which ends the scroll and the fling of its release, as in `#navigate` | C-097: Contents from the right edge |
